scene: Day 62, late afternoon at a water-treatment plant. Seen from just inside a wide-open metal sliding gate: a thick bright yellow line painted across the concrete yard with three huge yellow arrows pointing left. A group of round-headed survivors runs in and turns left along the arrows; one thin man with a stethoscope around his neck pushes an old lady sitting very straight on a wheeled office chair. Right behind them a dense crowd of green walkers in torn clothes pours through the gate and keeps walking straight ahead toward the edge of a huge basin of dark green water, under a pole with a red siren. Patch (round white head, black dot eyes, orange bandage on the forehead, orange backpack) presses his back against the wall next to the gate, close to the camera, eyes huge, one sweat drop. Tense because one wrong turn and the living walk into the water with them.

Night inside a glass control booth high above a water-treatment plant. Ines (round white head, bright yellow hooded raincoat) clutches a small handheld radio with both hands, eyes shining. Patch (round white head, orange bandage on the forehead, orange backpack) leans in beside her, his mitten hand pressing the talk button, mouth open in surprise. A long wire runs from the radio up through a small window. Through the glass, far across a dark river, a tall dark apartment building; between them, a long bridge packed with green walkers. Emotional and tense because she is alive on the other side and the bridge is full.
